patterns: Design: hash map plus linked list

parts.title: Start here
parts.summary: How to use this guide, study plans, Big-O, C++ for problem solving, and a method for solving any problem.

chapters.title: How to Use This Guide
chapters.scope: What is in the repo, how chapters are laid out, how to study a chapter, how to run the code, how to review with spaced repetition, how to track progress with the README checklist.

chapters.title: Study Plans
chapters.scope: Plans for 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 6 months, with a day-by-day table of chapters and problems. What to skip when time is short. Which parts are T1 only. Daily routine.

chapters.title: Big-O From Zero
chapters.scope: Why count steps. Big-O, Omega, Theta in plain words. Counting steps in loops with small examples: single, nested, dependent, halving, harmonic. Log explained from zero. Recursion trees and the Master theorem with small examples. Amortized analysis with the doubling array. Space complexity and the call stack. Best, average and worst case. Complexity of all STL containers. Common complexity classes with how far each scales. The constraints table: which n allows which complexity (10, 20, 100, 500, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e9). Hidden costs: string concat, substr, erase, passing by value. 30 small code snippets where the reader guesses the complexity, with collapsible answers.

chapters.title: C++ and the STL for Problem Solving
chapters.scope: Setup: compile and run with g++ on Windows. Why bits/stdc++.h, and why GCC 16 needs an explicit cassert include. Integer sizes, overflow, long long, INT_MAX, unsigned size_t traps, integer division, floating point compare. vector, string, array, pair, tuple, structured bindings. stack, queue, deque, priority_queue with min-heap and custom comparators. set, multiset, map, multimap, unordered_set, unordered_map: operations, complexity, when to choose which, the erase-one-from-multiset trap, operator[] inserting keys. Custom hash for pair. Algorithms: sort with lambda, stable_sort, reverse, unique, lower_bound, upper_bound, binary_search, min_element, max_element, accumulate, count, find, iota, fill, next_permutation, nth_element, partial_sort, rotate, partition, gcd, lcm. Bit helpers: __builtin_popcount, __builtin_clz, __builtin_ctz, bitset. String helpers: substr, find, stoi, to_string, isdigit, isalpha, tolower, stringstream to split. Lambdas and recursive lambdas with std::function. Pass by reference. Fast input and output. Reading all HackerRank-style input formats. Common compile errors and runtime errors and what they mean. Every section has a small runnable example.

chapters.title: How to Solve Any Problem
chapters.scope: The step-by-step method for a live interview: understand and restate, ask clarifying questions (list them), make examples, find the brute force, find what is slow (bottleneck, unnecessary work, repeated work), pick a better tool, plan in words, code, test by hand, state complexity. Exact phrases to say out loud. What to do when stuck. How to test code by hand with an edge-case list. Time plan for 30, 45 and 60 minutes. Two complete worked sessions shown as a script with interviewer and candidate lines, one Easy and one Medium. Common mistakes in communication.

chapters.title: Logic Building Warm-Ups
chapters.scope: The small tasks used as entry filters at software houses and in campus tests. Star and number patterns: right triangle, pyramid, diamond, Floyd triangle. Number tasks: count digits, reverse a number, palindrome number, Armstrong numbers, perfect numbers, all divisors in O(sqrt n), prime check, primes up to n, factorial, Fibonacci, sum of a series. Array tasks: max, min, second max, sum, reverse, count even and odd. String tasks: count vowels, count words, character frequency, reverse words. Matrix tasks: sum of rows, transpose. Each has a tiny program, and each builds the habit of tracing a loop by hand.

chapters.title: Amortized Analysis
chapters.scope: Why the cost of one operation can mislead. The three methods on the same two examples: aggregate, accounting and potential, on a stack with multipop and a binary counter. Dynamic table that grows and shrinks: why halving at half full thrashes, and why shrinking at one quarter works. Where amortized bounds appear: vector, two-stack queue, Union-Find, splay trees, monotonic stack.

parts.title: Pattern recognition
parts.summary: The heart of this guide: how to read a problem and know which technique to use.

chapters.title: How to Recognize Any Problem
chapters.scope: The 6-step reading procedure. Step 1 constraints give the complexity budget. Step 2 input shape. Step 3 what the output asks for. Step 4 keyword signals. Step 5 list candidates. Step 6 test each candidate with its validity question. A one-page master flowchart in Mermaid. Worked on 5 problems.

chapters.title: Constraints Tell You the Algorithm
chapters.scope: How to read n. A table from n to the allowed complexity to the likely techniques. Small n means exponential or bitmask. n about 500 means O(n^3) interval DP or Floyd-Warshall. n about 1e5 means O(n log n). n about 1e9 means O(log n), math or binary search on the answer. Value ranges and what they suggest: small alphabet, values up to 1e5 mean counting or a Fenwick tree, k small, sum small means knapsack. Examples for each row with real problems.

chapters.title: Decision Tree by Input Type
chapters.scope: One Mermaid decision tree plus explanation for each input type: unsorted array, sorted array, string, two strings, linked list, stack-like input, binary tree, BST, graph, grid, intervals, a number or digits, a stream of data, a design request. Each leaf links to a chapter. Also include: a list of queries, a permutation of 1 to n, points on a plane, a tree given as edges, a graph that is only implied by the rules.

chapters.title: Decision Tree by Question Goal
chapters.scope: One decision tree per goal: find a value, find a pair or triple, contiguous subarray questions, subsequence questions, count the ways, min or max cost, is it possible, list all solutions, top k, next greater or smaller, shortest path, ordering with dependencies, connectivity, range queries, palindromes. Each leaf links to a chapter.

chapters.title: Keyword Dictionary
chapters.scope: An alphabetical dictionary of phrases that appear in problems, at least 150 entries, each mapping to the likely pattern, why, and a chapter link. For example: 'contiguous', 'at most k', 'k-th largest', 'all permutations', 'minimum number of steps', 'overlapping intervals', 'next greater', 'in place', 'without extra space', 'sorted', 'rotated', 'parentheses', 'prerequisites', 'cycle', 'modulo 1e9+7', 'number of ways', 'subsequence', 'stream', 'median', 'prefix'.

chapters.title: Pattern Cards
chapters.scope: One compact card for every pattern in the curriculum's patterns list: when to use, the giveaway signal, a template of 5 to 15 lines, time and space, three classic problems, the most common mistake, a link to the chapter. Designed for fast revision. Group related patterns on one card when that is clearer, so that the file stays fast to revise.

chapters.title: Lookalike Patterns: How to Tell Them Apart
chapters.scope: Side-by-side comparisons of patterns that are easily confused, each with a decision rule and a problem pair that differs by one word: sliding window vs prefix sum vs two pointers vs Kadane; fixed vs variable window; DP vs greedy vs backtracking; DFS vs BFS vs Dijkstra vs Bellman-Ford vs Floyd; 0-1 BFS vs Dijkstra; topological sort vs cycle detection vs DFS; Union-Find vs DFS; heap vs sorting vs quickselect vs bucket sort; monotonic stack vs monotonic queue vs heap; binary search on answer vs DP vs greedy; subset vs permutation vs combination; 0/1 vs unbounded knapsack; LIS vs LCS; trie vs hash map; segment tree vs Fenwick vs prefix sum vs sparse table; subarray vs subsequence vs subset; memoization vs tabulation; Kruskal vs Prim; KMP vs Z vs rolling hash; fast and slow vs two pointers.

chapters.title: Worked Recognition Walkthroughs
chapters.scope: 40 real problems read out loud as an expert would: the first read, what the constraints say, the candidates considered, which were rejected and why, the final choice. Shows the inner monologue. Easy to Hard, across all topics.

chapters.title: Recognition Drills: Easy
chapters.scope: 100 short problem statements. The reader names the pattern before opening the collapsible answer. Each answer gives the pattern, the exact giveaway words, and a chapter link. Mixed order, so the reader cannot guess from the neighbours.

chapters.title: Recognition Drills: Medium
chapters.scope: 120 short Medium-level problem statements in the same format, mixed order. Include disguised problems where a story hides the real question.

chapters.title: Recognition Drills: Hard
chapters.scope: 80 short Hard and Expert-level problem statements in the same format, mixed order, including problems that combine two patterns. Explain how the two parts fit together.

chapters.title: When You Do Not Recognize the Problem
chapters.scope: A checklist of 20 moves for a problem you cannot place: solve small cases by hand, write the brute force and find repeated work, sort the input, think in reverse, think of the complement, fix one variable, add a dimension to the state, binary search the answer, model it as a graph, ask what would make it easy, reduce to a known problem, look for invariants, try greedy and find a counter-example. Each move has a real example.

chapters.title: When to Use Advanced Structures
chapters.scope: A ladder from plain interview problems to the advanced structures. For each structure (segment tree, lazy segment tree, Fenwick tree, sparse table, sqrt decomposition, Mo, persistent structures, order statistics tree, treap, binary lifting, heavy-light decomposition, centroid decomposition, suffix array, suffix automaton, Aho-Corasick, flow, matching, FFT): the plain problem that first needs it, the signal in the statement, what fails with simpler tools, and a chapter link.

parts.title: Arrays, strings and hashing
parts.summary: The building blocks that appear in almost every problem.

chapters.title: Arrays From Zero
chapters.scope: Memory layout and why indexing is O(1). Static vs dynamic arrays. Implement a DynamicArray class with push_back, pop_back, insert, erase, resize by doubling, and explain amortized O(1) with small numbers. 2D arrays and row-major layout. Basic algorithms: reverse, rotate, find max and second max, linear search. In-place vs extra space. Running minimum and running maximum idea. Boyer-Moore voting.

chapters.title: Strings From Zero
chapters.scope: Characters as numbers, ASCII math such as c - 'a'. The C++ string and the cost of each operation. Substring vs subsequence vs subset. Palindrome and anagram checks. Building strings efficiently. Parsing numbers from strings. Big-number string arithmetic.

chapters.title: Hash Tables From Zero
chapters.scope: What a hash function does, with a hand example. Buckets and collisions. Full implementation of separate chaining. Full implementation of open addressing with linear probing, tombstones for deletion, then quadratic probing and double hashing. Load factor and rehashing. Why average O(1) and worst case O(n). unordered_map vs map. Anti-hash attacks and a custom hash. Hashing a pair or a vector. Choosing keys for a hash map. Cuckoo hashing as a short note.

chapters.title: Hashing Patterns
chapters.scope: Four core uses of a hash map: seen before (set), complement lookup, frequency counting, grouping by a canonical key. How to choose the key. Index maps. Pair counting in one pass: count pairs i < j with a property as you scan. Frequency of frequencies: a second map that counts the counts.

chapters.title: Matrix Problems
chapters.scope: Row and column math. Direction arrays. Layer-by-layer traversal. Transpose and reverse for rotation. Using the first row as a marker. Diagonals: i + j and i - j. Staircase search. In-place state encoding. Sparse matrix forms: triplet form and compressed sparse row.

chapters.title: Simulation, Enumeration and Brainteasers
chapters.scope: Problems with no clever algorithm: do exactly what the statement says, carefully. How to model the state. Direction vectors and turning. Finding a cycle in a simulation to skip ahead. Enumeration: try all candidates, but choose what to enumerate so that the count is small. Brainteasers: invariants and parity. Constructive problems. Fix the middle element of a triple and multiply the counts on each side. Skipping ahead once a state repeats.
classic: Count Triplets: geometric progression with ratio r

chapters.title: String Parsing and Log Processing
chapters.scope: The most common online assessment task type. Splitting a line into fields. Parsing numbers, times and dates by hand. Grouping records by a key, sorting by time, aggregating. Date and time arithmetic: leap years, day of the week, days between dates, seconds since midnight. Validating formats. Robust handling of bad input. State machine parsing with a table of states.

chapters.title: Advanced Hashing
chapters.scope: Universal hashing and why a random hash function defeats attacks. Perfect hashing idea with two levels. Cuckoo hashing, full implementation. Robin Hood hashing idea. Zobrist hashing for game boards. XOR hashing to compare multisets. Keep this chapter short.
classic: XOR hashing to compare multisets in ranges

parts.title: Linked lists, stacks and queues
parts.summary: Every type: singly, doubly and circular lists; array and linked stacks; linear, circular and double-ended queues.

chapters.title: Singly Linked List
chapters.scope: Nodes and pointers explained from zero with ASCII diagrams. Why a list and when not. Full class with insertAtHead, insertAtTail, insertAtPosition, deleteHead, deleteTail, deleteAtPosition, deleteValue, search, get, length, print, reverse, and a destructor. Show the list state after every operation. The dummy node trick and why it removes special cases. Array vs linked list table. Reversal is shown as an operation; pattern depth lives in the reversal chapter.

chapters.title: Doubly Linked List
chapters.scope: prev and next pointers. Full class with insert and delete at both ends and at a position, delete a node in O(1), reverse, forward and backward traversal, and a destructor. Sentinel head and tail nodes. Comparison with singly linked. std::list. Why LRU needs a doubly linked list. XOR linked list as a memory-saving variant. Unrolled linked list and self-organizing list as short notes.
classic: Delete a node given only a pointer to it
Find pairs with a given sum in a sorted doubly linked list

chapters.title: Circular Linked Lists
chapters.scope: Circular singly linked list and circular doubly linked list. Why keep a tail pointer. Full classes for both: insert at front and back, delete, search, traverse without an infinite loop (do-while), destructor that breaks the loop first. Show the state after every operation. Uses: round-robin scheduling, media playlists, Josephus.
classic: Josephus problem with a list and with the recurrence
Split a circular linked list into two halves
Check whether a linked list is circular

chapters.title: Linked List Problems
chapters.scope: Recipes for list problems: dummy nodes, two lists at once, counting the length first, splitting and rejoining, hash map of nodes, weaving copies between originals. Assumes singly list basics.
classic: Flatten a linked list with bottom pointers
Sort a linked list of 0s, 1s and 2s
Quick sort on a linked list

chapters.title: Stack From Zero
chapters.scope: LIFO with a stack of plates. Full implementation with a fixed array (overflow and underflow), a growing array, and a linked list. std::stack. Function call stack. Two stacks in one array. k stacks in one array with a free list. Reverse a stack with recursion. Sort a stack. Min stack in two ways. When the problem wants a stack: most recent unmatched item, undo, nesting.
classic: Sort a stack using another stack
Insert at the bottom of a stack
Delete the middle of a stack

chapters.title: Stacks for Expressions and Parentheses
chapters.scope: Infix, prefix and postfix explained with hand conversions. Operator precedence and associativity. Infix to postfix (shunting yard), infix to prefix, evaluate postfix and prefix. Calculators with and without parentheses, sign handling. Parentheses family: matching, depth counters, index stacks, two-pass counting. Recursive descent parsing: one function per grammar rule, with a small calculator as the example.

chapters.title: Queue From Zero
chapters.scope: FIFO with a line at a bank. Naive array queue and why it wastes space. Linked list queue, full implementation with front and rear pointers. std::queue. Queue using two stacks with amortized analysis. Stack using one queue and two queues. When a problem wants a queue: process in arrival order, BFS, simulation by rounds. Types of queues overview table: linear, circular, deque, priority, monotonic, with links. In the types of queues table, add short notes on blocking queues, randomized queues and multilevel feedback queues.
classic: Generate binary numbers from 1 to n with a queue
Reverse the first k elements of a queue
Interleave the two halves of a queue

chapters.title: Circular Queue and Ring Buffer
chapters.scope: The wasted space problem. Modulo arithmetic for wrap-around, with a picture of each step. Full vs empty: count field vs one empty slot, both implemented. Full implementation. Ring buffers in real systems such as logging and audio. k queues in one array. Circular array traversal tricks with the modulo and the doubled array idea, and links to problems that use them.
classic: Circular queue with one empty slot
Moving average with a ring buffer
Bounded log buffer that keeps the last n entries

chapters.title: Deque: Double-Ended Queue
chapters.scope: Operations at both ends. Full implementation with a circular array and with a doubly linked list. std::deque and how it stores blocks internally. Input-restricted and output-restricted deques. When a problem wants a deque: both ends matter, sliding window extremes, 0-1 BFS.
classic: Implement a stack and a queue with a deque

chapters.title: Array-Based Lists and Memory
chapters.scope: Linked lists without pointers: next indexes inside an array, also called cursor-based lists. Free lists. Memory pools and why they beat new and delete in hot code. Header nodes. Short notes on garbage collection: reference counting and mark and sweep. Keep this chapter short.
classic: A fixed-size memory pool with a free list

parts.title: Sorting and searching
parts.summary: All the sorting algorithms, every kind of binary search, and how sorting unlocks other techniques.

chapters.title: Elementary Sorts
chapters.scope: Bubble, selection, insertion and shell sort, each with a dry run table on a tiny array, full code, best, average and worst case, stability and when each is useful. What stable means with an example. A comparison table. Cocktail, comb and gnome sort as short notes. Timsort as a short note on what real libraries use.

chapters.title: Merge Sort
chapters.scope: Divide and conquer picture, the merge step by hand, full code, recursion tree analysis for O(n log n), stability, space. Bottom-up merge sort. External sorting idea. The counting trick: during merge you can count pairs across the two halves.
classic: Merge two sorted arrays without extra space
New Year Chaos: minimum adjacent swaps with a limit per person

chapters.title: Quick Sort and Quickselect
chapters.scope: Partition by hand. Lomuto and Hoare schemes. Why pivot choice matters, random pivot, worst case. Three-way partition and the Dutch national flag. Quickselect for the k-th element and why it is O(n) on average. Median of medians idea. nth_element. Comparison with merge sort and introsort. The median minimizes the sum of absolute differences, with a short proof by moving the point.
classic: Second largest in n + log n comparisons

chapters.title: Counting, Radix and Bucket Sort
chapters.scope: Why comparison sorts need n log n, with a decision tree picture. Counting sort, stable version with prefix sums. Radix sort LSD and MSD. Bucket sort. When each applies. Heap sort is in the heap chapter.

chapters.title: Sorting With a Custom Order
chapters.scope: Comparators and lambdas in C++. Strict weak ordering and why a wrong comparator crashes. Sort by multiple keys. Sort indices rather than values. Sort then greedy. Sort then scan. How to discover the right order with the exchange idea.

chapters.title: Binary Search Basics
chapters.scope: Guess-the-number game. The invariant. Three templates: find exact, lower bound, upper bound. Why mid = low + (high - low) / 2. Termination and off-by-one rules. lower_bound and upper_bound in C++. Rotated arrays: which half is sorted. Peaks: binary search with no sorted order. Median of two sorted arrays.
classic: K-th element of two sorted arrays

chapters.title: Binary Search on the Answer
chapters.scope: The big idea: if checking an answer is easy and answers are monotonic, binary search the answer. Writing the can(x) function. Minimize the maximum and maximize the minimum. Choosing bounds. Floating point answers. Finding the k-th smallest with a count function.

chapters.title: Other Searching Algorithms
chapters.scope: Linear search and sentinel search. Jump search. Exponential search. Interpolation search. Ternary search on unimodal functions, and its integer form. Golden section idea. When each applies.
classic: Ternary search on a unimodal array

chapters.title: External Sorting and Sorting Networks
chapters.scope: Sorting data that does not fit in memory: external merge sort, replacement selection, k-way merge with a loser tree. Sorting networks: comparators, bubble network, Batcher odd-even idea, why they suit parallel hardware. What real libraries use: introsort, Timsort, pdqsort. Cycle sort and pancake sort. Keep this chapter short.

parts.title: Core patterns
parts.summary: The patterns that solve most interview problems: two pointers, sliding window, fast and slow pointers, prefix sums, monotonic structures, heaps and more.

chapters.title: Two Pointers: Opposite Ends
chapters.scope: Why sorted order lets you discard one element per step. Pair sum, triple sum, closest sum. Skipping duplicates. Water and area problems. Why it is correct, with a proof by elimination.

chapters.title: Two Pointers: Same Direction
chapters.scope: Read pointer and write pointer. Filtering in place. Two sequences at once (subsequence check, merge). Writing from the back. Comparison with sliding window. Run-length grouping: find each block of equal neighbours with an inner while loop.

chapters.title: Fast and Slow Pointers
chapters.scope: The tortoise and the hare. Why they must meet, with a small proof. Finding the cycle start, with the math explained simply. Finding the middle and why the loop condition decides which middle. Hidden linked lists: happy number, array as next pointers. Combination with reversal for palindromes. Brent's algorithm as a short note.

chapters.title: Sliding Window: Fixed Size
chapters.scope: Add one, remove one. Why it beats recomputing. Templates with sum, frequency table and matches counter. Anagram windows. Picking from both ends turned into a middle window.
classic: First negative integer in every window of size k

chapters.title: Sliding Window: Variable Size
chapters.scope: Already written as the model chapter, with P1 to P9. Extend it with the listed problems, keeping the voice and format exactly. Keep existing content.

chapters.title: Prefix Sums
chapters.scope: Running totals. Range sum in O(1). The prefix array off-by-one. 2D prefix sums with inclusion-exclusion, with a picture. Prefix sum plus hash map for exact targets and negative numbers. Remainders and modulo tricks. Turning 0 and 1 into -1 and +1. Prefix XOR. Prefix and suffix arrays. Prefix bitmask: one parity bit per letter.
classic: Count subarrays with XOR equal to k

chapters.title: Difference Arrays and Sweep Line
chapters.scope: Range add in O(1), then one pass. Difference array as the inverse of a prefix sum. Sweep line with events, sorting events, tie-breaking of starts and ends. Counting overlaps. Skyline with a multiset. Using a map as a sparse difference array. 2D difference arrays. Forced greedy: the leftmost wrong position forces an action, and a difference array tracks open actions.

chapters.title: Kadane's Algorithm
chapters.scope: Maximum subarray: extend or restart. Why it works, as DP with one state. Returning the subarray itself. Maximum product with min and max. Circular arrays. Allowing one deletion. Kadane on rows for a 2D maximum sum rectangle.
classic: Maximum sum rectangle in a 2D matrix

chapters.title: Merge Intervals
chapters.scope: Overlap test with a picture of all six cases. Sort by start. Sort by end for scheduling. Merge, insert, remove, intersect. Greedy interval scheduling and its link with activity selection. Heap of end times.

chapters.title: Cyclic Sort and Index as Hash
chapters.scope: Numbers in range 1 to n: each number has a home. Place each number at its index with swaps, why that is O(n). Negative marking. Finding missing and duplicate numbers with O(1) space. Math and XOR alternatives. Permutation cycles: minimum swaps to sort equals n minus the number of cycles.
classic: Minimum swaps to sort an array

chapters.title: In-Place Linked List Reversal
chapters.scope: Three pointers, drawn step by step. Iterative and recursive reversal. Reverse a sublist. Reverse in groups. Swap pairs. How to reconnect the ends safely.

chapters.title: Monotonic Stack
chapters.scope: Next greater element with a stack of unresolved items, drawn step by step. Why each element is pushed and popped once. Four variants: next or previous, greater or smaller. Storing indexes vs values. Histogram areas. Contribution technique: count subarrays where an element is the minimum, ties handled with one strict and one non-strict side. Greedy removal to build the smallest string.

chapters.title: Monotonic Queue
chapters.scope: Sliding window maximum: why a heap is not needed. A deque of useful candidates, drawn step by step. Why it is O(n). Min and max queues together. Prefix sums plus monotonic deque for negative values. Using it to speed up DP.

chapters.title: Top K With Heaps
chapters.scope: When a heap beats sorting. Min-heap of size k for the k largest, and why it is min and not max. Comparators in priority_queue. Top k frequent with heap and with bucket sort. Greedy with a heap: always take the best now. Task scheduling.

chapters.title: Two Heaps
chapters.scope: Median by keeping a max-heap of the low half and a min-heap of the high half. Balance rules, drawn step by step. Removing from a heap with lazy deletion. Sliding window median with multisets. Maximizing capital with two heaps.

chapters.title: K-Way Merge
chapters.scope: Merging k sorted lists with a heap of the current heads. Why O(N log k). Lazy generation of sorted answers, treating a matrix or a set of pairs as k sorted lists. Ugly numbers.

chapters.title: Bit Manipulation
chapters.scope: Binary from zero. AND, OR, XOR, NOT, shifts, with a truth table. Set, clear, toggle, check bit i. x & (x - 1) and x & -x, drawn in binary. XOR facts. Two's complement. Bitmasks as sets and enumerating subsets of a mask. Counting bits per position. Builtin functions. XOR of 1 to n by the n mod 4 pattern. Swap without a temporary. Subarray OR, AND and GCD: only about log V distinct values end at each index.

chapters.title: Contribution Technique
chapters.scope: When a problem asks for a sum over all subarrays, subsequences or pairs, stop looping over the groups. Ask instead how much each single element adds to the total. Counting how many subarrays contain index i. Using the last occurrence of a character. Sorted order for subsequence widths. Per-bit contribution. Combining with a monotonic stack.

chapters.title: Ordered Set Patterns
chapters.scope: std::set, multiset and map as searchable sorted containers, taught as a pattern. Nearest value above or below with lower_bound. Keeping a sliding window in a set. Keeping the min and max of a changing group. Picking the next free item. Interval bookkeeping in a map. Compare with heaps and sorted arrays, and when each is better. The erase-one-from-multiset trap.

chapters.title: Offline Query Processing
chapters.scope: When all queries are known up front, you may answer them in any order. Sort the queries, sweep once, and write answers back by original index. Offline with a heap, with Union-Find, with a Fenwick tree. Two-condition queries. Parallel binary search idea.
classic: Count distinct values in ranges with an offline Fenwick tree

chapters.title: Transform the Input
chapters.scope: Tricks that turn a hard problem into a known easy one. Reverse the process. Count the complement. Separate the variables: rewrite a condition so that each side uses one index. Remove absolute values by trying each sign. Coordinate compression. Map values to ranks. Turn a condition into a sum of +1 and -1. Each trick has a before and after picture.

chapters.title: Left and Right Scans
chapters.scope: Compute something from the left, compute something from the right, and combine at each index. Prefix max and suffix max. Best answer to the left of i. Fix the middle and combine both sides. Links to Trapping Rain Water, Product Except Self and Candy as members of this family.

chapters.title: Interactive Problems
chapters.scope: Problems where you get an API and a limit on the number of calls. How to test them in C++ with a mock. Binary search through an oracle, with links to First Bad Version and Guess Number. Candidate elimination: each call removes one candidate. Minimax: choose the query whose worst answer leaves the fewest candidates. Reading and flushing in contest-style interactive judges.
classic: Find a hidden number with a limited number of queries

parts.title: Recursion, backtracking, divide and conquer, greedy
parts.summary: How to think recursively, how to search all choices, and when a simple choice is enough.

chapters.title: Recursion From Zero
chapters.scope: A function that calls itself, with the call stack drawn by hand. Base case and progress. How to trust the recursion. Head vs tail recursion. Recursion trees. Stack overflow and limits. Recursion vs iteration. Writing a recursive solution in three steps.
classic: Print all binary strings of length n

chapters.title: Backtracking: Subsets
chapters.scope: The universal template: choose, explore, unchoose, drawn as a decision tree. Include or exclude vs for-loop style. Handling duplicates by sorting and skipping. Subsets by bitmask. Counting 2^n.

chapters.title: Backtracking: Permutations and Combinations
chapters.scope: Permutation vs combination vs subset, in one small picture. Used array vs swap method. Start index for combinations. Skipping duplicates with the sorted-and-used rule. Reuse of elements. Generating parentheses. The k-th permutation by math.

chapters.title: Backtracking: Constraint Search
chapters.scope: Search with pruning. Checking validity early. N-Queens with diagonal arrays. Sudoku. Word search on a grid. Partitioning strings. k-partition with memo. Expression insertion. Branch and bound with a knapsack example.

chapters.title: Divide and Conquer
chapters.scope: Split, solve, combine. The Master theorem applied. Maximum subarray by divide and conquer. Closest pair of points. Karatsuba multiplication. Strassen idea. Expression evaluation by splitting at each operator. Compare with DP: subproblems do not overlap.
classic: Maximum subarray by divide and conquer

chapters.title: Greedy Foundations
chapters.scope: Make the best local choice and never look back. When it works: greedy choice property, optimal substructure. How to prove it: exchange argument and stays-ahead, on small examples. How to break a wrong greedy with a counter-example. Greedy vs DP on coin change. Reach extension: with sorted values, the reachable range grows until a gap appears. A short note on matroids as the general reason greedy works.

chapters.title: Classic Greedy Algorithms

parts.title: Design problems
parts.summary: Problems that ask you to build a class: caches, iterators, schedulers, and small systems.

chapters.title: LRU and LFU Cache
chapters.scope: What a cache is. How to find the design: list the operations, then pick structures to make each O(1). LRU with a hash map plus doubly linked list, drawn step by step. std::list with iterators. LFU with frequency buckets. O(1) all-one structure.

chapters.title: Stack and Queue Design Problems
chapters.scope: Extra operations on stacks and queues. Lazy updates. Grouping by frequency. Two structures that stay in sync.

chapters.title: Iterators
chapters.scope: hasNext and next. Lazy work: do only what the next call needs. Peeking. Flattening with a stack. Zigzag. BST iterator. Run-length iterator.

chapters.title: Hashing and Randomized Design
chapters.scope: Array plus index map for O(1) random pick. Swap with last to delete. Time-based key-value store with binary search. Rate limiting. Hit counters. Event tracking with maps.

chapters.title: System-Style Design Problems
chapters.scope: Small systems as classes. How to list operations and data. Twitter feed. Tic-tac-toe with O(1) moves. Snake. File system with a trie. Autocomplete. Spreadsheet. Parking. Food ratings. Log storage. Fancy sequence with modular math. Text editor with two stacks. Rate limiter: token bucket, sliding window.

chapters.title: Concurrency Basics
chapters.scope: Threads and why order is not guaranteed. Race conditions, shown by a broken counter. std::mutex, lock_guard, unique_lock. Condition variables and the wait loop. Semaphores. Deadlock and the four conditions. Producer and consumer with a bounded blocking queue. Read-write locks. The LeetCode Concurrency problems. Tests must be deterministic: join all threads and assert the final result, never rely on sleeping.

parts.title: Interview practice
parts.summary: Ranked problem lists, timed mock sets and last-minute revision.

chapters.title: The Must-Do 100
chapters.scope: The 100 highest-value problems in a suggested order, each linked to where this repo solves it, with its pattern and a one-line reminder of the key idea.

chapters.title: Famous Problem Lists Mapped to This Guide
chapters.scope: The problems from widely known lists (Blind 75, NeetCode 150, Grokking patterns), each with a link to where this repo solves it. Use the repo's chapter links. Include a checklist. Cover Blind 75, NeetCode 150, NeetCode 250, Grind 75, LeetCode 75, LeetCode Top Interview 150, Striver SDE Sheet, Striver A2Z, Love Babbar 450 and the Grokking patterns, as far as they can be recalled accurately. Add an alias table for classic names, such as Connect Ropes for Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks. Problems not solved in this guide get a one-line hint.

chapters.title: Online Assessment Playbook
chapters.scope: How HackerRank, Codility and similar assessments work. Reading input in C++ for each format. Time strategy. Partial credit. Common question types at Pakistani software houses and at international companies. Debugging without an IDE. A full worked example of a stdin problem. Progressive multi-level tasks, as on CodeSignal, where each level adds rules to the same code.

chapters.title: Mock Interview Sets
chapters.scope: 30 timed sets, each with 2 to 3 problems of rising difficulty, mixed topics, linked to the solutions. Grouped as screening, on-site Medium, and on-site Hard. Include a scoring rubric.

chapters.title: Edge Cases and Testing Checklist
chapters.scope: Edge cases by input type: arrays, strings, numbers, linked lists, trees, graphs, grids, intervals. How to write test cases fast. How to dry run your own code. How to stress test with a brute force.

chapters.title: Common Bugs and How to Find Them
chapters.scope: Overflow, off-by-one, unsigned size, iterator invalidation, modifying a container while looping, map operator[] side effects, uninitialized variables, integer division, recursion limits, comparator bugs, TLE causes, MLE causes. Each with wrong code and right code. How to read Runtime Error, TLE, WA and MLE messages.

chapters.title: Template Cheat Sheet
chapters.scope: All the core templates in one file, each a compact, tested program: binary search variants, sliding window, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, Union-Find, topological sort, trie, segment tree, Fenwick, KMP, DP skeletons, fast power, sieve.

chapters.title: Last-Night Revision
chapters.scope: A 30-minute read before the interview. The recognition checklist, the key complexity facts, the top 20 tricks, what to say at each step, how to stay calm.

chapters.title: Online Assessment Tasks Mapped
chapters.scope: The Codility lessons and the HackerRank Interview Preparation Kit, topic by topic, each task mapped to the chapter and technique that solves it, with a one-line hint. Include the warm-up tasks that software houses use as filters.
